Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Guidage radar?

In this glossary, Guidage radar refers to: Heading instructions issued to provide navigational guidance by radar

How is Guidage radar used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "United 345, virez à gauche cap 270, guidage radar pour espacement en approche finale."

Why does Guidage radar matter in aviation?

Guidage radar matters because it supports clear communication in Basic ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Guidage radar?

Guidage radar is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

What category does Guidage radar belong to?

In this glossary, Guidage radar is grouped under Basic ATC. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ICAO Doc 9432, FAA PCG and published by Protermify Aviation as a static aviation reference page.

Definition

Heading instructions issued to provide navigational guidance by radar

Operational example

United 345, turn left heading 270 degrees, vectors for traffic spacing to final approach course.

Localized term

Localized example
